title: tidy's process records name the dispatching session, a forged record is never removable, and a reused pid's record is cleared
goal: dispatch records its worker's pid with the dispatching session and the worker's start time, so tidy --class process can end a finished worker; a process record whose pid is not a process this clone's tools started (pid 1, a pid whose command is no claude or tool run) is never listed as remove; a record whose pid now names another process (start time differs) is cleared, not kept for ever

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print("check failed:", e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import os, subprocess, tempfile, json, time
T = os.path.realpath(tempfile.mkdtemp())
ENV = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(("GIT_", "KB_COORD"))}
ENV.pop("CLAUDECODE", None)
ENV.update(KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(T, "coord.sqlite"), GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1",
           GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="t@example.com", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="t@example.com")
def g(*a, cwd):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=cwd, env=ENV, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
def tool(*a, ok=(0,), env=None):
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, *a], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env or ENV, timeout=300)
    assert r.returncode in ok, (a, r.returncode, r.stdout[-800:], r.stderr[-800:])
    return r
O, C = os.path.join(T, "origin.git"), os.path.join(T, "clone")
g("init", "-q", "--bare", "-b", "main", O, cwd=T)
g("clone", "-q", O, C, cwd=T)
os.makedirs(os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog"))
open(os.path.join(C, "backlog.json"), "w").write('{"item_dir": "kb/_self/backlog"}\n')
open(os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog", ".keep"), "w").close()
g("add", "-A", cwd=C); g("commit", "-qm", "base", cwd=C); g("push", "-q", "origin", "main", cwd=C); g("fetch", "-q", cwd=C)
own = lambda p, cls, *a: tool("_tools/backlog.py", "--root", C, "own", str(p), "--class", cls, *a)
def rows(*a):
    r = json.loads(tool("_tools/backlog.py", "--root", C, "tidy", "--json", *a).stdout)
    return r["rows"] if isinstance(r, dict) else r
own(1, "process", "--session", "s-fake")
rs = [x for x in rows("--class", "process", "--older-than", "0") if x.get("class") == "process"]
v = {x.get("pid"): x.get("verdict") for x in rs}
assert v.get(1) != "remove", ("a forged record makes pid 1 removable", v)

notes: SP-ipeewrlv review (S2): dispatch records the worker process with no --session (bl_dispatch.py:957), so process_verdict keeps it for ever and the process class never ends a dispatched worker; `own 1 --class process --session s-fake` lists pid 1 (launchd) as would remove, and the operator's --apply would signal it; a reused pid is keep and its record is never cleared (bl_clean.py:405). The check plants only the forged-record case.
